about.heading: Every brief already contains its own answer. Most of it is just buried.
services.heading: Five disciplines. One buried premise.
services.web-dev.title: Web Development
services.web-dev.description: Websites and web applications built on foundations that don't shift under load. We write front-end and back-end code meant to be read by the next engineer, not just shipped by this one.
services.ui-ux.title: UI / UX Design
services.ui-ux.description: Product design grounded in how people actually behave, not how a moodboard wants them to. Research, design systems and prototypes that hold up once real content and real users arrive.
services.cyber.title: Cyber
services.cyber.description: Security woven into the build, not inspected in afterwards. We audit applications and infrastructure, close the gaps we find, and set up monitoring so the next gap gets caught early. No system is unbreakable — ours are built to fail safely and get noticed fast.
services.marketing.title: Marketing
services.marketing.description: Brand strategy and growth work that assumes people are busy and skeptical, because they are. We build campaigns, content and SEO foundations that earn attention instead of renting it, then prove it with numbers you can check.
services.devops.title: DevOps
services.devops.description: Cloud infrastructure and delivery pipelines that let you ship on a Friday without dread. Infrastructure as code, automated deployment and monitoring built so scaling up is a config change, not a re-architecture.

faq.heading: Before you ask.
faq.1.question: What does Emerald actually do?
faq.1.answer: We design and build digital products end to end — web development, product design, security, marketing and infrastructure — as one team rather than five separate hires.
faq.2.question: Can you work alongside our existing team?
faq.2.answer: Regularly. We slot into an existing team for a specific discipline — security audits and design systems are common entry points — and hand off cleanly with documentation your team can actually use.
faq.3.question: Do you build from scratch, or work with what we have?
faq.3.answer: Both. Most projects start with an audit of what exists so we're not rebuilding things that already work. What we replace, we replace on purpose.
faq.4.question: Do you offer support after launch?
faq.4.answer: Post-launch support, monitoring and improvements can be included in your proposal, with the scope and duration agreed before work begins.
faq.5.question: What technologies do you use?
faq.5.answer: We pick the stack to fit the problem rather than our own preferences — commonly modern JavaScript frameworks, cloud-native infrastructure and established, well-audited security tooling. We'll always explain the choice.
faq.6.question: How does a project actually start?
faq.6.answer: A short call to understand the problem, followed by a scoped proposal within a few business days. No lengthy sales process before you know roughly what it costs.
